quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road, and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: If you are on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center of the road, and the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass if no traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: What color are the lines that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines are used in the center of the road to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may go only when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians and it is safe to proceed.

questions.question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. It means you may pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What affects how quickly you can stop your car?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your stopping ability. Slow down on poor road conditions to keep control of your car. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and don't need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your car can cross the entire track without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross all the way across without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at or near a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under normal conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under normal conditions. You may drive slower, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather, or when conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: What color lines separate lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines may be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt normal traffic flow. You can receive a citation for driving too slowly.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: When pulling out of a driveway onto a street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly so people can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so people know you are coming.
Stop and check for pedestrians and vehicles before entering.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check for pedestrians and vehicles before entering.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming before you proceed.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: At high speeds, tires cannot clear water from the road. Your car may slide on water instead of gripping the road. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol will:

options.text: Not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce alcohol in your blood. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane meant for oncoming traffic. Only do this if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When parking uphill on an incline with a curb, turn your front wheels:
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed in the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Stay at freeway speed until you are on the exit ramp, then slow down.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: The blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is a blind spot around large trucks where the driver cannot see you. Stay out of these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in that direction.

questions.question: Your vehicle has no Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). To stop quickly, you should:
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly in an emergency. It lets you keep control and steer your vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving past a car that just parked on the side of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: Assume the driver will open the door as you pass. Drive carefully and use extra caution near parked cars.

questions.question: You stop completely at an intersection. You yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then you go when it is safe. This matches which traffic light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Roads freeze most quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on roads shaded by trees or buildings. These spots dry last.

questions.question: A driver with a Graduated Driver License:

options.text: Does not need to wear a seat belt.
Must follow the same rules as a regular driver license.
Cannot use any cell phone while driving.
Can use electronic devices while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot use any cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: A GDL driver cannot use any cell phone or electronic device while driving. All drivers must wear a seat belt.

questions.question: A driver age 21 or older on a GDL must practice supervised driving for at least ____ before taking the road test.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 on a GDL must practice for at least six months. Drivers age 21 or older on a GDL must practice for at least three months before the road test.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and look behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Can stop faster than passenger cars.
Do not need more room to turn than passenger cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind. Stay out of these areas. Trucks also need more space to turn and stop than passenger cars.

questions.question: What does this green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect how far it takes your vehicle to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: Your windshield wipers suddenly fail during rain or snow. What should you do?

options.text: Roll down the driver's window and put your head out to see ahead.
Stop and pull off the road.

questions.explanation: If your wipers fail in rain or snow, you should slow down, move to a safe area off the road, and turn on your emergency flashers. Call for help if you need it.

questions.question: You are driving on a busy street and your accelerator gets stuck open. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully so you don't lock the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully so you don't lock the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep going even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition by moving the switch just enough to stop the engine—not so far that it locks the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may go if the way is clear.
You must come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you drive past this sign, you are going the wrong way and may have a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you finish the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to the one you just left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet, slippery, or you cannot see well. When conditions are not perfect, drive slower than the posted speed limit. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you follow the speed limit.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel to work properly with your seat position.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to let cars know to move.
Drive around a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: During the probationary period with a special learner permit, how many points can you get before entering a Probationary Driver Program?
questions.explanation: During the two-year probationary period after getting a special learner permit, you cannot have more than four points from traffic violations. Two or more moving violations that total four or more points will require you to enroll in a Probationary Driver Program. If you do not complete the program, your license will be suspended.

questions.question: After your suspended license is restored, how long is the probationary driving period?
questions.explanation: After your license is restored, you will be on probation for one year. During this year, any moving traffic violation will cause your license to be suspended again.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a steady green light unless a sign says otherwise. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Drivers under 21 with a probationary license must display what on their license plate?
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 on a probationary license must display two visible GDL decals on their license plate. These reflective decals are provided by the Motor Vehicle Commission.

questions.question: When you approach an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident or disaster just to look.
